issues.detail: The Greek 'ο εχων βαλαντιον' refers to someone who *has* a purse/moneybag. The Vietnamese translation says 'ai có túi tiền, hãy lấy đi' (whoever has a moneybag, let them take it), which is not in the Greek text. The Greek implies a contrast between those who have the means and those who do not.

The Vietnamese translation repeats 'ai có cái túi' (whoever has the bag) as a separate clause, which is redundant and misinterprets the Greek structure where 'ο εχων βαλαντιον' is the subject of the first part of the contrast.
